messages:
mika: Heads-up — spotted intermittent Xid 13 + a flurry of single-bit ECC corrections on r-infra-gpu-07 during the overnight soak. Node went into drain automatically once NVML reported 120 corrected ECCs in 1h. Looking to lock down a reproducible burn-in workflow so we can confidently return cards to service instead of immediate replace.

sam: Thanks. Can you paste the quick NVML logs and the sequence that triggered the drain? Also curious if this is vram or cache errors.

mika: nvml excerpt:
```
Timestamp: 2026-03-17 03:12:14
GPU 0: Xid Error 13 (ECC single-bit corrections rising)
ECC corrected: 127 last hour
Thermal: 71C
Power draw: 245W
PCIe retries: 4
```
Looks like memory/corrected ECC spiking, not full ECC fatal. PCIe retries present but low. Root cause unknown — could be flaky DIMM on board or intermittent PCIe glitches.

jordan: Agree we should have a standard reproduce flow. Suggest steps: 1) repro in isolated rack (no tenant VMs), 2) stable power cycle, 3) run memtest + synthetic workload hitting big sequences + long-run attention-heavy generation. If it reproduces, run a longer soak.

mika: Draft burn-in checklist I'm proposing (short):
- Put node into maintenance + drain.
- Export NVML and dmesg.
- Power-cycle and run 30m memtestG (gpu-memtester).
- Run synthetic long-context generation (soakbench) with 1xA100 load + high sequence lengths for 4h.
- Run PCIe stress (pciestrict) for 30m.
- Collect nvml counters every 60s, sample logs to S3.
- If corrected ECC > 50 in 1h or Xid 13 repeats 2x => tag for replace/return.

sam: Can you post the soakbench and memtester commands? I'll script them into the node quarantine job.

mika: Put these in the thread as a starting point:
```
# memtester (GPU) - run on node host as root
gpu-memtester --device 0 --duration 30m --pattern heavy

# soakbench synthetic generator
soakbench --model llama-2-7b --seq-len 4096 --batch 8 --duration 4h --log-interval 60 --out /tmp/soak-$(hostname).log

# nvml polling (simple)
while true; do nvidia-smi --query-gpu=timestamp,ecc.corrected.volatile,ecc.pending --format=csv >> /var/log/gpu-ecc.log; sleep 60; done &
```

ops-bot: CI job gpu-quarantine-run started for r-infra-gpu-07 (job id: 98321). Will post run artifacts to: s3://redwood-gpu-debug/98321/

jordan: Nice. For thresholds: I'd set soft-warning at 20 corrected ECC / hour, hard at 50. For Xid count: 1 Xid 13 is tombstone but not immediate replace; >2 distinct Xid 13 events inside a 6h window => retire. Thoughts?

alyssa: Also note capacity: r-infra-gpu-07 is in us-west-2-dedicated pool. If we quarantine it, we need to trigger autoscale fallback to keep SLAs. Sam, can the quarantine job mark the pool capacity as -1 so autoscale will spin up burn seats? We should avoid impacting production routes.

sam: Yep, I'll add a hook to the quarantine job to call the autoscale API: POST /internal/autoscale/adjust {pool: "us-west-2-dedicated", delta: 1}. We'll only trigger if pool availability < 5%.

diego: What about thermal cycling? A few cards fail only after extended thermal cycles. Add a 3x hot-cold loop (60m soak at 75C, then cool). If errors correlate with thermal changes, that's a shipping-quality hardware issue.

mika: Good call. Add thermal-cycle: power high-load 45m then forced fan reduction for 20m, repeat 3x, capture temps. Also we should capture BMC logs and PCIe slot counters before shipping back.

sre-oncall: Assigning to me for the initial run. I'll kick the quarantine job at 10:00 UTC and attach the artifact link here. If we get reproducible >50 ECC or Xid repeat, I'll follow replace workflow and open a replace-ticket with vendor vendor-ops (cc: diego).

mika: Thanks. One more: if memtester fails non-deterministically, don't automatic replace — escalate to hardware bench team first. Some cards recover after reseating/thermal cycling.

jordan: Documented. I'll update the runbook in Confluence with the commands and thresholds above. Link back here for traceability.

sre-oncall: Quarantine job started: https://ci.redwood.internal/job/98321. Artifacts will appear in ~5m.

ops-bot: Artifact upload complete: s3://redwood-gpu-debug/98321/soak.log, nvml.csv, bmc.log

sre-oncall: Early results: memtester showed intermittent failure at 12m, nvml shows 63 corrected ECCs in first hour and one Xid 13. Moving to thermal-cycle next. Will report final conclusion in this thread.

mika: Perfect — thanks for running it. If it reproduces, we'll follow retire/replace. If it doesn't, keep node quarantined for 24h and re-run nightly soak for 4 nights before return. :white_check_mark:
